processing: Orthodox-style black tea from the garden's own leaf and bought-in smallholder leaf; a white tea is also made.
harvest_season: Little is documented for this garden; as elsewhere in the eastern Nepali hills, spring and autumn lots are the ones usually sought.
appearance_dry: Twisted dark leaf with golden tips in the tippy grades.
appearance_liquor: Clear amber, as is usual for Nepali orthodox black tea.
appearance_wet: Mixed coppery-brown leaf, as is usual for a Himalayan orthodox tea.
taste_profile: The gold-tipped black is described as fruity; the white tea as full-bodied, with hay, floral and muscatel notes.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for Himalayan orthodox tea. Cooler water suits the white tea and any spring lot.

vintage_note: Sold in small lots through specialist importers, usually under a grade or lot name such as Makalu Tippy rather than a long-running label. As with other Nepali orthodox teas, buy the current year's lot and drink it fresh; old lots do not improve.
description:
Kuwapani is a tea plantation in Dhankuta in the hills of eastern Nepal, counted with Guranse and Jun Chiyabari among the district's three best-known gardens. It grows its own tea and buys leaf from nearby smallholders.

It turns out black tea, including tippy gold-tipped lots, and a white tea. Beyond that, little is published about its methods or fields.

The descriptions that exist are of individual lots: a fruity black, and a full white with hay and muscatel notes. Brew either like a Darjeeling, with cooler water than you would give a strong black.

The name turns up mostly on importers' lists, so you may have to look for it. Compare it with Guranse for a sense of how the same district differs by garden.
history:
The garden's history is thinly documented. A Himalayan Times report of June 2005 gives Kuwapani Tea Plantation a processing capacity of 40,000 kg, smaller than Guranse and Narayani, and says it had begun producing tea only that year.

A retired Makalu Tippy lot from 2012 shows the name was already in export trade by then. Dhankuta was declared a tea zone in 1982 along with neighbouring districts.
